metadata.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Backport vllm-project/vllm#56576, #59565, #59126: broken-EXIF image hashing, GLM-5.3-Flash image budget and vision rope table
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Backport of three upstream vLLM fixes for image inputs, one commit each, in the same form as the earlier backports #657 (vllm-project/vllm#44082) and #1406 (vllm-project/vllm#60472). main does not have them. vllm-project/vllm#44974 (EXIF orientation and tRNS transparency), which we carry on our fork as well, is on main through #1310 and #1366 and is not part of this PR. None of the three changes depends on the GPU; the second and third concern the GLM-5.3-Flash vision part (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration, vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/), which main already serves with images.

1. vllm-project/vllm#56576 (9ca6dbba7, by Ama Senevirathne), "tolerate malformed EXIF metadata during hashing". MultiModalHasher (vllm/multimodal/hasher.py) called getexif() unguarded to look for an ImageID. For an image whose EXIF block has no valid TIFF header, Pillow raises SyntaxError there, and the request fails with HTTP 500 after the image itself loaded. The hasher runs for every image a client sends without a uuid (vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py). Since #1310, load_bytes keeps such images (normalize_image suppresses the EXIF error), but a P-mode PNG with a broken eXIf chunk still fails in the hasher, because the mode conversion hands it a fresh image that parses the EXIF again. The helper _get_image_id_bytes and the Image.Image hunk apply unchanged; the MediaWithBytes hunk is placed by hand, because the io_config branch from upstream #49975 does not exist here. The upstream test uses normalize_image from #1310 instead of repeating its suppress, and hash_kwargs without the algorithm argument; an added test covers the chat API path (load_bytes, then hashing) for RGB, RGBA and P PNGs. As upstream and as #1310 for loading, a broken EXIF block does not fail the request: the image comes from the client, the hasher reads EXIF only for an optional ImageID, and the hash then covers the image data or the original bytes.

2. vllm-project/vllm#59565 (5688a4dd4, by Yufeng He), "[GLM-5.3] Size the image encoder cache from the exact token ceiling". Glm5NextProcessingInfo (vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/multimodal.py) inherits the square probe of Glm4vProcessingInfo.get_image_size_with_most_features, which refits 9999999x9999999 to 2492x2492, that is 89x89 = 7921 tokens, below the checkpoint ceiling of 8000 (max_image_tokens in processor_config.json). The encoder cache is sized from it, so every image of 7922 to 8000 tokens is refused with HTTP 400. On main with the nvidia GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 checkpoint the registry gives 7921 tokens per image (profiling image 2492x2492), while the processor turns a 3840x2160 screenshot into 7973 tokens and a 3840x2880 photo into 7931. We hit it in production on our fork, which has the same code: the boot log says "Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 7921 tokens", and a 3840x2160 screenshot was refused with "The decoder prompt contains a(n) image item with 7973 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921." The method is inserted unchanged behind _get_video_max_pixels (the patch did not apply because the file differs from upstream around it). The upstream test uses build_model_context on zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash and a test file this repository does not have; instead tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_budget.py runs the real Glm5NextImageProcessor with the checkpoint settings and checks the encoder-cache maximum (get_mm_max_tokens_per_item) against the processed token counts. The profiling dummy grows from 2492x2492 to 2800x2240 (31,684 to 32,000 patches); images that were accepted before are processed as before.

3. vllm-project/vllm#59126 (097989299, by Juan Calderon-Perez), "[Multimodal] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash vision tower crashes on image input". The vision tower built its rotary table with 8192 rows, and rot_pos_emb indexes it by grid row and column. The image processor does not bound the aspect ratio, so a wide or tall image gets a longer side: a 200000x20 image has 14,286 patches along one side, and the image budget allows up to 16,000. The lookup then reads past the table, a device-side assert that kills the engine. Upstream sizes the table from max_position_embeddings of the text config, which for GLM-5.3-Flash is 1,048,576 rows, 64 MiB in fp16 on the first pipeline stage. Here the table covers the longest grid side the processors can emit: max_grid_side() derives it from the pixel budget smart_resize keeps (a canvas one aligned cell high and the whole budget wide), and the model takes the larger value of the image processor (16,000 at 8000 tokens) and the video processor (60,000 under its 30,000-token serving cap), 3.66 MiB in fp16 instead of 0.5 MiB. To read both processors without loading the tokenizer, Glm5NextProcessor.from_pretrained now delegates to the new media_processors_from_pretrained. The budget lookup of Glm5NextProcessingInfo became the module function _processor_pixel_budget, shared with max_grid_side; both stay in the model package, so the generic processor module gains no model coupling. The first 8192 rows are computed as before, so existing grids get the same cos/sin values. The other part of the upstream PR (staging pos_ids and cu_seqlens through pinned memory for VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK) is left out: this repository has no VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK, and its async_tensor_h2d takes a list. Known limit: the table size comes from the checkpoint's processor config, so raising max_image_tokens above 30,000 through --mm-processor-kwargs can again produce a grid side longer than the table, which upstream's 1,048,576 rows would still cover.

The GLM commits do not depend on #1286 (open), which changes the same file for quantized vision weights and row chunking. If #1286 is merged first, the only overlap is its comment on _ROWS_PER_CHUNK, which names 31,684 patches as the largest image; with #59565 that becomes 32,000.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs of this repository for 56576, 59565, 59126, 44974, EXIF, "malformed EXIF", hasher, "encoder cache size", "GLM-5.3 vision", "GLM image", "image budget", "rope table" and "vision tower", and the issues for the same terms. #1310 and #1366 (merged) cover #44974, which is why it is not here; #1363 (merged) keys partial prefix entries on image identity, a different change. #1260 (open) changes the pixel budget of Glm5NextProcessingInfo for per-modality processor overrides; it does not touch get_image_size_with_most_features or the rotary table, but both PRs edit _processor_pixel_budget (here it becomes a module function), so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. #1365 (open) changes the Glm4v dummy video frame search (the "max_pixels=47040000 is too small" failure of issue #631) and encoder profiling under pipeline parallelism, independent of this PR. No PR or issue covers #56576, #59565 or #59126.

AI assistance was used for this backport. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py tests/multimodal/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image_alpha.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image_orientation.py tests/transformers_utils/processors/test_glm5next.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_budget.py tests/models/glm5next/test_mtp_config.py tests/models/glm5next/test_pp.py
The new tests against main's sources (git checkout origin/main -- vllm/ in the branch, then back): test_hasher.py and the test_vision_budget.py of the #59565 commit.
On CPU with the nvidia GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 checkpoint: get_mm_max_toks_per_item through MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor (max_model_len 524288, limit_mm_per_prompt image 12), on main and on this branch; rot_pos_emb of the vision tower with 8192, 16,000 and 60,000-row tables on grids [1, 2, 14286], [1, 2, 16000] and [1, 80, 100].
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
End to end on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, prod-v6f 0b342e7b5, which carries these three commits; GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 PP5 over three V100 and two RTX 8000, --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":12,"video":0}', temperature 0): a 3840x2160 PNG screenshot and a 3840x2880 JPEG photo, each showing one number, asked for the number; a P-mode PNG whose eXIf chunk has no TIFF header (after convert("RGB") Pillow raises SyntaxError in getexif()); a 20x200000 strip, then a text-only request. The screenshot also against the same tree without the bundle (our previous production, prod-v6e) in the bundle A/B.

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MultiModalHasher (vllm/multimodal/hasher.py) | image hashing | PIL image or MediaWithBytes whose EXIF block has no valid TIFF header | ImageID used when readable; otherwise the hash covers the image data or the original bytes, as for images without EXIF | executed: tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py (JPEG, and RGB, RGBA, P PNGs through load_bytes) | none known |
| Glm5NextProcessingInfo.get_image_size_with_most_features (GLM-5.3-Flash) | encoder cache budget, profiling dummy | checkpoint max_image_tokens 8000, or a max_pixels override | budget equals the processor ceiling (8000); profiling image 2800x2240 | executed: tests/models/glm5next/test_vision_budget.py; registry on the GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 checkpoint on CPU | none for the image sizes tested (see Test Result) |
| Glm5NextVisionTransformer rotary table (GLM-5.3-Flash) | vision rotary embedding | grid sides up to 16,000 patches (image) and 60,000 (video, 30,000-token cap) | table of max_grid_side rows; first 8192 rows unchanged | executed: test_vision_budget.py; rot_pos_emb on CPU | video at the 30,000-token cap |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fix, not a performance change.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664; the same changes run on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, prod-v6f at 0b342e7b5).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none for the tests.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. The fork tree with these commits and the other upstream backports of the same bundle passed an A/B/A/B of our GLM-5.3-Flash PP5 entry (with images) and our DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 entry against the trees without them: prefill, decode, GSM8K-30 and eight quality texts unchanged on both models (texts token-identical). On GLM, the boot logs of the three test arms say "budget of 8000 tokens" (the two arms without the fixes: 7921), and the test arms answered the image probes (3840x2160 screenshot 8002 prompt tokens, 3840x2880 photo 7960, an EXIF-rotated 1080x1440 photo 2057, the number in each image read correctly); the two arms without the fixes refused the screenshot with the encoder-cache error quoted above.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these three commits):
- First test command: 134 passed.
- Second test command: 16 passed, 2 failed. The failures, test_pp.py::test_glm53_materialized_mhc_state_crosses_pp_boundary and test_pp.py::test_glm53_dflash_aux_hidden_states_cross_pp_boundary (AttributeError: 'Glm5NextModel' object has no attribute '_pp_aux_dump'), fail the same on main c98a8d664; this PR does not touch test_pp.py or that code.
- The new tests against main's sources: test_hash_image_malformed_exif and test_hash_loaded_png_with_malformed_exif[P] fail in test_hasher.py, and 4 of the 5 tests in the #59565 version of test_vision_budget.py fail (7973, 7931 and 7973 tokens above the 7921 budget, ceiling 7921 instead of 8000). With the #59126 commit the test module does not import on main (no max_grid_side).
- Registry on the GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 checkpoint (CPU): main 7921 tokens per image, profiling image 2492x2492; this branch 8000, 2800x2240. Processor tokens unchanged: 3840x2160 7973, 3840x2880 7931, 2160x3840 7973, 640x480 414.
- rot_pos_emb on CPU (fp16): with 8192 rows, grids [1, 2, 14286] and [1, 2, 16000] raise IndexError ("index 8192 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 8192"); with 16,000 rows both pass. The first 8192 rows of the 16,000 and 60,000-row tables are bit-identical to the 8192-row table, and cos/sin for the [1, 80, 100] grid are bit-identical between 8192 and 60,000 rows.
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py (platform coupling 25 -> 32) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (37 -> 39); this PR touches neither file, the report is the same on main c98a8d664.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.

End to end on our fork as in the test plan: the screenshot is accepted with 8002 prompt tokens and the photo with 7960, and both numbers are read correctly; without the bundle the same screenshot fails with "The decoder prompt contains a(n) image item with 7973 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921." The PNG with the broken eXIf chunk is answered (1448 prompt tokens, number read correctly); this shape is test_hash_loaded_png_with_malformed_exif[P], which fails against main's sources (above). The 20x200000 strip is answered (7167 prompt tokens: "Das Bild zeigt ein extrem schmales, hohes Schwarz-Weiß-Muster ..."), and the text request after it is answered correctly (17 x 23 = 391), so the engine keeps serving.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
